projects.title: Business Maps (newplace.city)
projects.description: Non-commercial hex-grid map overlaying competitor density, estimated client demand, and Department of Finance storefront rent data so business owners and analysts can screen locations. Runs on a monthly data-refresh cycle and was shown at BetaNYC's Civic Tech Summer Showcase on August 20, 2026.
projects.why_interesting: Combines three normally siloed NYC Open Data layers, competition, demand, and rent, into one screening tool, and the builder is openly soliciting methodology feedback rather than presenting it as finished.

projects.title: CityScroll
projects.description: Searchable interface unifying the City Record with PASSPort, Checkbook NYC, and community board postings, filterable by neighborhood, agency, topic, and keyword, with multilingual support and email alerts. Built by James Carroll and Michael Sheehan, with the data pipeline updated through August 2026.
projects.why_interesting: The City Record is notoriously hard to parse; this is the first tool in this scan that cross-links it to procurement and land-use data in a single search.

projects.title: Parking Reimagined
projects.description: Interactive tool letting residents drop templates onto a standard parking space to visualize alternative uses, costs, and land-use tradeoffs, with a printable workshop kit for community board discussions. Built by Gibson Chu and debuted at the August 20, 2026 BetaNYC Summer Showcase.
projects.why_interesting: A participatory-design visualization built for community board meetings rather than a passive browsing dashboard.

projects.title: Good Standing
projects.description: Badge-based platform rewarding volunteer civic action with artist-designed badges redeemable at local businesses, built by Ashley Taylor to help nonprofits coordinate volunteers. Shown at the August 20, 2026 BetaNYC Summer Showcase.
projects.why_interesting: Less a data project than a civic-engagement mechanism, but one that could generate a participation dataset worth watching as it grows.

projects.title: IBO Monthly Fiscal Indicators Dashboard, FY27
projects.description: The Independent Budget Office's recurring tracker of monthly fiscal indicators for fiscal year 2027, flagged in BetaNYC's August 20, 2026 newsletter.
projects.why_interesting: An official, nonpartisan fiscal-monitoring dashboard that serves as a baseline for any city-finance story.

projects.title: CodeNOW NYC
projects.description: Free hosting and infrastructure platform, a local branch of the Czech CodeNOW network, letting volunteer-run civic tech projects move from demo to production without managing their own servers. Built by Matt Keough and shown August 20, 2026.
projects.why_interesting: Addresses a chronic failure mode in civic tech, good tools dying after the demo, by supplying the infrastructure layer rather than another dataset.

projects.title: Philadelphia Litter Index Map
projects.description: Philly Plain Dealer, working with the nonprofit We Love Philly, mapped the city's 2024-2025 Litter Index dataset block by block, showing dump locations, litter scores, and in some cases what was dumped. Published September 1, 2026.
projects.why_interesting: A local outlet turning an under-used city dataset into a direct-to-neighborhood accountability map, a useful model for local-journalism-sourced finds rather than government or nonprofit releases.

projects.title: College Station Interactive Planning Map
projects.description: City-run interactive map combining the Future Land Use and Character, Thoroughfare, and Bicycle and Pedestrian plan layers with platting, zoning, and property data. Published September 3, 2026.
projects.why_interesting: A smaller-city example of consolidating multiple planning-data layers that most cities still keep as separate static PDFs.

projects.title: DataIndex.us
projects.description: Federation of American Scientists project monitoring federal dataset health, tracking Office of Management and Budget information change requests, survey and form changes open for public comment, and a terminations tracker for discontinued data collections. Flagged in BetaNYC's September 4, 2026 newsletter.
projects.why_interesting: Surfaces upstream risk to the federal inputs, American Community Survey, Bureau of Labor Statistics data, that city dashboards depend on.

projects.title: hpd-lookup
projects.description: Open-source tool that translates New York City Department of Housing Preservation and Development housing-violation codes into plain English and flags roughly 59,000 problematic or malformed records in the raw open dataset. Featured in BetaNYC's August 20, 2026 newsletter.
projects.why_interesting: Documents a specific, sizable data-quality problem in a widely used dataset that most users would not otherwise catch.

projects.title: BetaNYC: New-York-City-Budget
projects.description: Machine-readable, line-by-line reconciled City Council budget data, Schedule C discretionary funding for fiscal years 2009 through 2027, Terms and Conditions, Section 254 capital changes, and transparency resolutions, extracted deterministically from adopted-budget PDFs with no AI-inferred figures. The fiscal 2027 Schedule C total reconciles to exactly $655,764,999.
projects.why_interesting: Converts hundreds of PDF budget pages into clean, joinable tables, a rigorously verified structured version of NYC budget data that most reporting tools lack.
